[25] 1. For the purposes of this Agreement, Information means information relating to one party which is made available by such party to the other party for the Business Purpose, including but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples but excluding Information which:
[26] I. is publicly available or becomes publicly available (other than as a result of disclosure by the Receiving Party or any other person contrary to the terms of this Agreement; or
[27] II. was available (as can be demonstrated by the Receiving Party's written records or other reasonable evidence) to the Receiving Party or another person to whom it is furnished hereunder free of any restriction as to its use or disclosure prior to its being so furnished; or
[28] III. becomes available to the Receiving Party (as can be demonstrated by the Receiving Party´s written records or other reasonable evidence) from a source other than the Disclosing Party, which source is not bound by any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in relation to such Information; or
[29] iv. is independently developed by the Receiving Party;
[30] v. or is required to be disclosed, retained or maintained by law or any regulation or any governmental organization.
[31] Confidential Information may also be handed out by a third party appointed by the Disclosing Party (i.e. manufacturer).
[32] 2. Both Parties shall
[33] I. treat the Information with the same degree of care to avoid disclosure to any third party as is used with respect to the Receiving Party´s own Information of like importance which is to be kept confidential; Confidential
[34] II. keep the Information relating to the other party secret and confidential and not disclose any of it to any third person and only make it available to the Receiving Party´s executive board, directors, employees, advisers or subsidiaries and affiliates who need to know the same for the Purpose;
[35] III. use the Information only for the Business Purpose unless the Disclosing Party gives its prior written consent to such Information being used for some other agreed purpose;
[36] IV. keep the Information, relating to the Disclosing Party, and any copies thereof secure and in such way so as to prevent unauthorized access by any third party, nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form;
[37] V. ensure that its employees and advisers comply with the obligations of non-disclosure arising from this Agreement;
[38] 3. Either Party shall have the right to refuse to accept any Information under this Agreement prior to any disclosure and nothing herein shall obligate either Party to disclose any particular Information.
[39] 4. All Information exchanged between the Parties pursuant to this Agreement shall upon respective request of the Disclosing Party either be returned to the Disclosing Party or be destroyed.
[40] On request the Receiving Party shall supply a written certificate signed by any of its directors confirming the destruction of the Information.
[41] 5.
[42] The Information, relating to the other party, shall remain the property of such other party (as Disclosing Party) and its disclosure shall not confer on the other party (as Receiving Party) any rights.
[43] No license is hereby granted by either party to the other party, directly or indirectly, under any patent, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property.
[44] 6. The Parties disclaim any warranty for the correctness and completeness (including but not limited to warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement) regarding Information under this Agreement.
[45] 7. The Agreement shall continue in force for three years from the signing of this Agreement.
[46] Thereafter it shall automatically continue unless terminated upon thirty days prior notice in writing.
[47] The obligations accruing prior to termination as set forth herein, shall, however, survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of two years.
[48] 8. This Agreement shall be governed and construed by the laws of Singapore, without regard to any conflict of law principles leading to the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
[49] The Parties hereby submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Singapore.
[50] 9. If any of the provisions of this Agreement are or become wholly or partly void, invalid or unenforceable, this shall not affect the validity of the remaining provisions.
[51] The provisions of this Agreement may not be modified, amended, nor waived, except by a written instrument duly executed by the Parties hereto.
[52] The requirement of written form can only be waived in writing.
[53] 10. This Agreement may not be assigned by either party without the prior written consent of the other.
[54] 11. Insofar as one of the Parties undergoes a transformation by change in its legal form preserving its identity or by a change in legal personality due to merger, break up or transfer of assets this Agreement shall be continued with the newly formed legal successor or the legal successor taking over one of the Parties.

Hypotheses:
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-19: Survival of obligations - Segment [47] says "The obligations accruing prior to termination as set forth herein, shall, however, survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of two years." This entails the hypothesis. Evidence: [47].

nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure - Segment [30] mentions information "required to be disclosed, retained or maintained by law or any regulation or any governmental organization" as an exclusion, but there's no obligation to notify the Disclosing Party. NotMentioned.

nda-11: No reverse engineering - No mention of reverse engineering anywhere. NotMentioned.

nda-12: Permissible development of similar information - Segment [29] excludes information "independently developed by the Receiving Party" from the definition of Information. This entails that the Receiving Party may independently develop similar information. Evidence: [29].

nda-1: Explicit identification - No requirement that Confidential Information be expressly identified. NotMentioned.

nda-16: Return of confidential information - Segment [39] says "All Information exchanged between the Parties pursuant to this Agreement shall upon respective request of the Disclosing Party either be returned to the Disclosing Party or be destroyed." This is upon request, not upon termination. The hypothesis says "upon the termination of Agreement." Hmm, the document says "upon respective request" not "upon termination." This could be considered NotMentioned since the trigger is request, not termination. But some interpretations might consider this entailment. The hypothesis specifically says "upon the termination of Agreement" - the document says "upon respective request of the Disclosing Party." These are different triggers. I'd lean toward NotMentioned, but let me think. Actually, in many NDA audits, this is labeled as Contradiction or NotMentioned because the return/destruction is upon request, not upon termination. I'll say NotMentioned.

nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement - No mention of not disclosing the fact of the agreement. NotMentioned.

nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information - Segment [25] says Information includes "but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples" - "including but not limited to" means it's not only technical. This contradicts "shall only include technical information." Evidence: [25]. Contradiction.

nda-15: No licensing - Segment [43] "No license is hereby granted by either party to the other party, directly or indirectly, under any patent, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property." Also [42] "its disclosure shall not confer on the other party (as Receiving Party) any rights." Entailment. Evidence: [42], [43].

nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession - No mention of retaining information after return/destruction. NotMentioned.

nda-18: No solicitation - No mention of solicitation. NotMentioned.

nda-7: Sharing with third-parties - Segment [34] says "only make it available to the Receiving Party's executive board, directors, employees, advisers or subsidiaries and affiliates who need to know the same for the Purpose." Advisers could be third parties (consultants, professional advisors). This entails sharing with some third parties (advisers). Evidence: [34]. Entailment.

nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information - Segment [28] excludes information that "becomes available to the Receiving Party... from a source other than the Disclosing Party, which source is not bound by any obligation of confidentiality." This entails the Receiving Party may acquire similar information from a third party. Evidence: [28]. Entailment.

nda-5: Sharing with employees - Segment [34] allows making information available to "employees... who need to know the same for the Purpose." Entailment. Evidence: [34].

nda-17: Permissible copy - Segment [36] says "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form." This prohibits copies. The hypothesis says Receiving Party may create a copy in some circumstances. This contradicts. Evidence: [36]. Contradiction.

nda-4: Limited use - Segment [35] "use the Information only for the Business Purpose unless the Disclosing Party gives its prior written consent." Entailment. Evidence: [35].

nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information - Segment [25] defines Information as "information relating to one party which is made available by such party to the other party" - no restriction to written form. "including but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples." The broad definition "made available" could include verbal. Hmm, this is ambiguous. The definition doesn't explicitly mention verbal information. Some audits label this Entailment because "made available" is broad and there's no written requirement. Others say NotMentioned. Given the definition is broad ("information... made available by such party to the other party"), and exclusions don't require written form, I'd lean Entailment with evidence [25]. Actually, let me think more carefully. The hypothesis is "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information." The document defines Information broadly without restricting to written/tangible form. This suggests verbal information could be included. I'll say Entailment with [25].

Let me verify some of these with human feedback. Let me check nda-16 first since it's tricky.
